extra.message: Code Injection via eval() in seller-formula-cast-255 — Arbitrary Python code execution on the server, enabling full server compromise including data access, credential theft, and pivot to internal infrastructure. [verified: Query param `expr` passed directly to `eval()` at line 61; the `{'__builtins__':{}}` restriction is trivially bypassable via attribute introspection (e.g., `().__class__.__bases__[0].__subclasses__()`). No input validation or allowlist exists; the `_wrk_gate` token check only gates access, not the injection.]

OS Command Injection via seller-shell-probe-396 — Remote code execution on the server with the privileges of the application process, enabling data theft, lateral movement, or full system compromise. [verified: Query param `host` concatenated unsanitized into `os.system('ping -c 1 ' + host)` at line 103; no shell escaping, shlex, or input validation exists anywhere in the call chain. The `_wrk_gate` shared-secret gate prevents unauthenticated access but provides zero sanitization, so anyone with the token achieves direct RCE.]

Missing rate limiting on login, registration, and password-reset endpoints — Unrestricted brute-force attacks against user passwords on the login endpoint; unlimited password-reset request spam that could overwhelm users or be used for timing-based account existence probes; automated account creation abuse on the registration endpoint. [verified: Duplicate of finding [3]: the same codebase-wide search for rate-limiting mechanisms returned zero results; login (line 100), register (line 49), and password-reset/request (line 171) all lack any throttle, lockout, or rate-limit enforcement.]

Missing rate limiting on login, registration, and password-reset endpoints — Brute-force password guessing, credential stuffing at scale, denial of service via auth endpoint flooding, and accelerated account enumeration. [verified: A codebase-wide search for rate-limit, RateLimiter, slowapi, throttle, and limiter returned zero results; no middleware, dependency, or decorator enforces rate limits on any authentication endpoint (register, login, password-reset).]

Password reset token returned in API response in development mode — Account takeover of any user whose email is known, including admin accounts, by requesting a password reset and using the returned token. [verified: auth.py line 147-150 returns the raw password-reset token when ENVIRONMENT=='development' (the default in config.py line 16); the token can be used immediately via /password-reset/confirm to set a new password for the target user. No compensating control exists.]

Password reset token returned in API response in development mode — Complete account takeover — an attacker can trigger a password reset for any known user email and immediately receive the reset token in the API response, bypassing the need to access the user's email. The attacker can then set a new password and gain full access to the victim's account. [verified: Duplicate of finding [0]: the password_reset_request endpoint at auth.py returns the raw reset token when ENVIRONMENT=='development' (the default), enabling immediate account takeover without email access.]

Path Traversal / Arbitrary File Write in seller-dropbin-slot-022 — Arbitrary file write on the server filesystem, enabling configuration overwrite, code planting, or system compromise via `.bashrc`, cron, or service files. [verified: Query param `packet_ref` used unsanitized in `incoming_dir / packet_ref` at line 26 with no `resolve()`, `..` filtering, or path confinement; `write_bytes()` writes request body to attacker-controlled path, enabling arbitrary file write via traversal sequences.]

Path Traversal / Arbitrary File Write in seller-dock-shelf-394 — Arbitrary file write on the server filesystem, allowing overwrite of critical files, planting of malicious code or SSH authorized keys. [verified: Query param `name` used unsanitized in `BASE_EXPORT_DIR / name` at line 95 with no path traversal prevention; `write_bytes(body)` writes request body to attacker-chosen filesystem location via `../` sequences.]

Account enumeration via registration endpoint distinct responses — An attacker can enumerate valid user accounts on the platform, which facilitates targeted phishing, credential stuffing, and password brute-force attacks against known valid accounts. [verified: auth.py line 58 returns HTTP 409 'Email already registered' on duplicate email versus HTTP 201 on success, providing distinct status codes that trivially distinguish existing from non-existing accounts. No generic error message or rate limiting mitigates this.]

Log Injection via User-Controlled Body and Authorization Header in seller-wire-tally-213 — Log forgery enabling audit trail corruption, injection of false log entries to mislead investigations, and potential plaintext exposure of authentication tokens in log files. [verified: `logger.warning('ops tally body=%s bearer=%s', body, ...)` at line 57 logs raw request body (enabling CRLF log-line injection) and the `Authorization` header value (exposing JWT/API key secrets in plaintext log files). No redaction or input sanitization is applied.]

Server-Side Template Injection (SSTI) via seller-blurb-tile-321 — Cross-site scripting (XSS) via HTML response containing attacker-controlled JavaScript, enabling session hijacking, credential phishing, or defacement. [verified: Query param `card` is rendered via `Template('{{ card|safe }}').render(card=card)` at line 73 with `|safe` disabling auto-escaping; this is reflected XSS (not SSTI—the template string is hardcoded). No sanitization of `card`; `HTMLResponse` returns attacker-controlled HTML/JS verbatim.]

CORS Origin Reflection with Credentials in seller-origin-mirror-376 — Cross-origin data theft from authenticated users via attacker-controlled websites making credentialed requests to this endpoint. [verified: `Access-Control-Allow-Origin` echoes the client's `Origin` header verbatim at line 89 while `Access-Control-Allow-Credentials: true` is set at line 90; no origin validation or allowlist exists. Any origin can make credentialed cross-origin reads of the JSON response.]

NoSQL Injection in seller-mongo-lane-416 — Unauthorized data access, data exfiltration from MongoDB, query logic bypass, or denial of service via resource-intensive regex queries. [verified: Request body JSON `filter` field passed directly as MongoDB query to `find_one(query)` at line 121 with no operator allowlisting or input filtering. An attacker can inject `$where`, `$regex`, `$ne` operators to bypass query logic or extract data.]

Hardcoded default JWT/HMAC secret key enables full authentication bypass — Complete authentication bypass — attacker can forge JWT session tokens for any user (including admins), forge password reset tokens, and derive API key hashes, leading to full account takeover and unrestricted access to all roles and data. [verified: Same hardcoded SECRET_KEY in config.py:10 as finding 0, used identically for JWT signing and HMAC peppering; exploitable only when env vars are absent, but the default is present and reachable via get_settings().]

Hardcoded default SECRET_KEY used for JWT signing and HMAC peppering — Attacker can forge session tokens for any user including admins, compute password reset and API key hashes, gaining full platform compromise. [verified: config.py:10 hardcodes a default SECRET_KEY used directly by create_session_token() and hash_token() in security.py; pydantic-settings reads env vars/.env first, but if neither is set in production the well-known default forges JWTs and HMACs for any user.]

Content-Security-Policy header not set in security middleware — The application lacks the primary browser-enforced mitigation against XSS and data injection. If any XSS vulnerability were introduced (e.g., via a missed sanitization, new feature, or third-party dependency), there is no CSP to restrict script sources, inline scripts, or data exfiltration destinations. [verified: The secure_headers middleware (main.py:47-52) sets X-Content-Type-Options, Referrer-Policy, and X-Frame-Options on every response but omits Content-Security-Policy entirely; the only CSP reference codebase-wide is seller_operations.py:125 which sets it to an empty string. React auto-escaping and bleach sanitization (security.py:98) provide primary XSS defense, making CSP absence a defense-in-depth]

Session cookie Secure flag disabled when ENVIRONMENT is development — Session hijacking via network sniffing or MITM attacks when the application runs in development mode on a network without TLS. [verified: auth.py line 34 sets secure=False when ENVIRONMENT=='development' (the default in config.py line 16); if the app is deployed without changing ENVIRONMENT and without TLS, session cookies are sent over cleartext HTTP. httponly and samesite=lax are already set, providing partial mitigation.]

Account enumeration via timing side-channel in login endpoint — Attacker can discover valid user emails, enabling targeted phishing, credential stuffing, and combined with the password reset token exposure, targeted account takeover. [verified: auth.py line 110 short-circuits: when the user is None, bcrypt.checkpw() is never called, creating a measurable timing delta vs. when the user exists. No constant-time guard or artificial delay is applied for non-existent users.]

Missing authentication gate on internal ops endpoint — Unauthenticated access to an internal operations endpoint that should be gated behind x-internal-token, violating the trust boundary for ops endpoints. [verified: seller_margin_fold_024 at line 38 genuinely lacks the _wrk_gate Depends() dependency present on all other /ops/* endpoints, making it reachable without x-internal-token; the endpoint exposes internal ops memo data (renewal risk, payment flags, owner contact details) without any authentication.]

Open Redirect in seller-return-lane-146 — Phishing attacks that leverage the trusted marketplace domain to redirect victims to attacker-controlled sites, enabling credential harvesting or malware distribution. [verified: Query param `lane` passed unsanitized to `RedirectResponse(lane)` at line 44 with no URL validation, allowlisting, or scheme restriction. An attacker with the internal token can redirect victims to arbitrary external URLs for phishing.]

Hardcoded demo account credentials in login page source — Anyone viewing the login page source can obtain valid credentials for all four role accounts (admin, vendor, support, buyer), enabling full compromise of the marketplace including admin-level access if the seed script has been run. [verified: Login.jsx line 50 embeds all four demo emails and password 'Marketplace1!' in JSX rendered in the page source, visible to anyone loading the login page. The seed.py script creates matching real database accounts with these exact credentials and the admin role, and the README instructs users to run seed during setup — so any deployment following the documented flow exposes valid privileged credenti]
